PV-02.c01: Once the bus is loaded and moving, you are responsible for the **riders** as well as the road.
A **charter carrier** rents out a bus and driver to a group; an **intercity carrier** runs buses between cities.
A **convex mirror** curves outward and shows a wider area than a flat mirror.
A **brake-door interlock** on some transit buses holds the bus still while the rear door is open.
PV-02.c02: Explain the rules about **smoking, drinking, or electronic devices** at the **start of the trip**, which helps avoid trouble later.
While driving, **scan the inside of the bus** as well as the road ahead, to the sides, and to the rear.
You may need to remind riders about the rules or to **keep their arms and heads inside** the bus.
PV-02.c03: Riders can **stumble** getting on or off and when the bus starts or stops, so tell them to **watch their step** when leaving.
**Wait for riders to sit down or brace themselves** before you start, and start and stop as smoothly as possible.
Keep a **drunk or disruptive rider** safe as well as the others; never let them off where it would be unsafe for them.
It may be safer to let them off at the **next scheduled stop** or in a **well-lit area** where there are other people.
PV-02.c04: Bus accidents often happen at **intersections**; stay careful **even when** a signal or stop sign controls the other traffic.
Leaving a stop, school and transit buses can **clip mirrors or strike passing cars**; watch your clearance, poles, and tree limbs.
Know the **gap** you need to speed up and merge, and **wait for it**; never assume other drivers will brake to make room.
PV-02.c05: Deadly bus crashes on curves come from **too much speed**, often when rain or snow makes the road slippery.
The **posted curve speed is set for cars** and can be too fast for many buses, even in good weather.
Too fast with **good traction** → the bus may **roll over**; with **poor traction** → it may **slide off**. Leaning outward on a banked curve means too fast.
Check mirrors quickly and regularly, never too long; **convex mirrors** show a wider area but make things look **smaller and farther away**.
PV-02.c06: Stop **between 15 and 50 feet** before a railroad crossing; look and listen both ways, and **open the forward door** if it helps you see or hear.
After a train passes, make sure **no other train** is coming on other tracks; with a manual transmission, **never change gears** while crossing.
No stop needed (slow down and check): street tracks in business/residence districts, **streetcar** crossings, a **peace officer or flagman**, a **green signal**, "exempt" or "abandoned" crossings.
Figure 4-A: tracks through an intersection with an official traffic signal are **exempt**; tracks with their own crossing warning device are **not exempt**.
PV-02.c07: Stop at a drawbridge that has **no signal light and no traffic control attendant**.
Stop **at least 50 feet** before the draw, and make sure the draw is **completely closed** before you cross.
No stop needed (slow down and make sure it is safe) with a **green light** or an **attendant or traffic officer** who controls traffic when the bridge opens.
Don't mix them up: railroad crossing = **between 15 and 50 feet**; drawbridge = **at least 50 feet**.
PV-02.c08: **Inspect your bus at the end of each shift**.
**Interstate** carrier drivers write a **report for each bus**, naming it and listing defects that affect safety or cause a breakdown; with no defects, the report **says so**.
Report rider damage to **handholds, seats, emergency exits, and windows** so mechanics can fix it before the bus goes out again.
**Mass transit** drivers also check that passenger signaling devices and **brake-door interlocks** work properly.
PV-02.c09: Fuel with riders aboard only if you truly must, and **never inside a closed building** with riders aboard, because fumes can catch fire.
**Do not talk with riders** or do anything else that distracts you while driving.
Don't tow or push a disabled bus with riders aboard **unless getting off would be unsafe**; then only to the **nearest safe spot** to let them off.
PV-02.c10: Urban mass transit buses may have a **brake and accelerator interlock**.
With the **rear door open**, it **puts on the brakes** and holds the throttle at **idle**; it releases when you close the rear door.
**Never use the interlock in place of the parking brake**, because it lets go as soon as the rear door closes.
